clue.text: Dead end that is restricting motorway progress

indicators.note: to restrict something is to hem it in, so one piece closes around the others

blocks.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, Latin for that is
M is the British road prefix for a motorway, as in the M1
to pass is to move on or progress

explanation.surface: A frustrating traffic jam on the motorway where nothing moves forward.
explanation.walkthrough: The I and E of i.e. go round M and PASS, giving IMPASSE.
explanation.definitionFit: An impasse is a situation with no way forward, literally or figuratively a blind alley.

clue.text: Funds raised in pub for vindaloo?

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising something lifts it so its letters read from bottom to top
placing something in another word means it sits inside that word

blocks.note: aid is money or funding given to help
an inn is a pub

explanation.surface: Money collected at the local to pay for a curry night.
explanation.walkthrough: Raised suits a down clue, where the letters climb the column. The question mark flags that vindaloo is only one example of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage an Indian is a meal from an Indian restaurant, and vindaloo is a fiery curry dish typical of one.

clue.text: Courteous drunk Edgar Allan entertains

indicators.note: a host who entertains has guests inside the house, so one piece holds another

blocks.note: Edgar Allan Poe, the American writer
lit is slang for drunk

explanation.surface: A tipsy Edgar Allan Poe proves a gracious host to his guests.
explanation.walkthrough: Drunk looks like it describes Poe, but it supplies its own piece, LIT, which Poe's surname wraps around.
explanation.definitionFit: Polite and courteous are straightforward synonyms meaning well mannered and respectful towards others.

clue.text: Twinkling, a son's green eye?

indicators.note: something twinkling flickers and moves about, so these letters shift into a new order

blocks.note: the letters taken as printed, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A mother admiring her boy's sparkling green eyes.
explanation.walkthrough: Twinkling seems to describe the eye, but it works on the letters. The question mark marks eye as one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The eye is the body part for sight, one example of the organs that detect stimuli from the world.

clue.text: Some sausages sent for German city

indicators.note: some means only a part, so the letters come from a stretch inside the following words

blocks.note: the run of letters across the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: A batch of sausages is shipped off to a city in Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs from the tail of sausages into sent; the sausage-and-Germany surface is apt.
explanation.definitionFit: Essen is an industrial city in the Ruhr area of western Germany, so a proper-name example.

clue.text: See 18
Similar articles on record: ring us

blocks.note: two articles: the indefinite AN and A
a log is a written record
O is ring-shaped
taken as written

explanation.surface: Matching items listed in a file with a request to phone.
explanation.walkthrough: Articles is plural, so it supplies two of them, AN and A; 'on' just places them before the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Analogous describes things comparable in certain respects, so it is a close synonym of similar or alike.

clue.text: Mysterious brunette

blocks.note: first meaning: secret, hidden, obscure
second meaning: having brown or black hair

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a description of an enigmatic woman, but the two words are separate meanings of one short word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means obscure or secretive, as in a dark secret, and also describes deep-coloured hair or complexion.

clue.text: Good old criminal keeping cash in chips

indicators.note: keeping something means holding on to it, so one piece holds another inside

blocks.note: O is the standard abbreviation for old
bent is British slang for crooked or corrupt
to cash in one's chips is an idiom for to die

explanation.surface: A veteran gangster hoarding his casino winnings.
explanation.walkthrough: Cash in chips looks like gambling, but the idiom means to die. Good is the definition in the sense of a well-behaved child or dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A good child or pet does as told, so here the sense is well behaved and compliant.

clue.text: Queen no longer duty-bound to use gym?

indicators.note: something bound is tied up and enclosed, so one piece is wrapped by another

blocks.note: Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen's cipher, no longer current under a king
excise is a tax or duty on goods

explanation.surface: A retired monarch, freed of official duties, can finally hit the gym.
explanation.walkthrough: No longer looks like it means ex, but it tells us the Queen is the late Elizabeth, whose ER sits inside the duty.
explanation.definitionFit: Working out at a gym is physical exercise; the question mark flags a playful, verb-like definition by description.

clue.text: Thomas, or Bob, or Lynda going out

indicators.note: going out suggests being disordered or knocked out of shape, so the letters rearrange

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Three people deciding which of them will head out for the evening.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas and Bob are both definitions: the Welsh poet Dylan Thomas and the singer Bob Dylan.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is shared by the Welsh poet, as his first name, and the American songwriter, as his surname.

clue.text: Get French cheeses picked up for doctor

indicators.note: to pick something up is to hear it, as a radio picks up a signal

blocks.note: to get a joke is to see it; Brie is a soft French cheese

explanation.surface: Collecting a cheese order on behalf of the family doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: Doctor seems to be a medic, but in Australia and South Africa a cooling afternoon onshore wind is called the Doctor, as in the Fremantle Doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: The Fremantle Doctor and Cape Doctor are local names for the refreshing wind blowing in from the ocean.

clue.text: With everything considered, when to retire?

annotation.answer: AT THE END OF THE DAY

blocks.note: first meaning: a stock phrase for when all is weighed up
second meaning, taken literally: the time to go to bed, at nightfall

explanation.walkthrough: Retire suggests leaving work, but the playful sense is going to bed, which happens when daylight is over.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a cliché meaning ultimately or all things considered, and literally names the evening, bedtime.

clue.text: Variable edge not hard in metal

indicators.note: not means without, so a letter is left out of the word before it

blocks.note: algebra uses x, y and z for unknowns
to edge forward is to inch forward
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: An adjustable blade fitted to a metal tool.
explanation.walkthrough: Edge is a verb here, meaning creep forward slowly; drop its H.
explanation.definitionFit: Zinc is a bluish-white metallic element used for galvanising steel, so it is one example of a metal.

clue.text: Church resident possibly given title

indicators.note: possibly signals one of several arrangements, so the letters may be reordered

blocks.note: CH is the standard abbreviation for church
taken as written

explanation.surface: A parishioner who might be honoured with a title.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a knighthood or similar honour, but given title just means named.
explanation.definitionFit: To christen is to give a name at baptism, and more loosely to name anything, so a title was bestowed.

clue.text: Dramatist appears to embrace supreme dynasty

indicators.note: an embrace wraps arms around someone, so one piece encloses another

blocks.note: to arise is to appear or come up
top means best or supreme
the Han dynasty ruled China for about four centuries

explanation.surface: A playwright seems to welcome a ruling royal house.
explanation.walkthrough: Appears is the outer word, not a link; it wraps around TOP and the Chinese dynasty.
explanation.definitionFit: Aristophanes was the great comic playwright of ancient Athens, author of The Frogs and The Birds.

clue.text: Pavlovian response leaving one in religious hope?

indicators.note: leaving here means going away, so a letter departs from the word

blocks.note: Pavlov's dogs famously drooled at the sound of a bell
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A conditioned reflex drawing someone away from their faith.
explanation.walkthrough: Pavlov trained dogs to drool at a bell; remove the I from that drooling.
explanation.definitionFit: Deliverance of the soul from sin is the central hope of Christian believers; the question mark marks a descriptive definition.

clue.text: More sticky as it were when dancing

indicators.note: dancers move around and change places, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone getting clammy, so to speak, out on the dance floor.
explanation.walkthrough: As it were seems a filler phrase, but it is the letter supply.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweaty skin feels clammy and tacky, so the comparative of perspiring fits the comparative more sticky.

clue.text: Play safe with hammer

blocks.note: peter is old criminal slang for a safe, so a safecracker is a peterman
to hammer a show is to pan it, criticising it harshly

explanation.surface: Instructions to play it safe while using a hammer.
explanation.walkthrough: Play looks like a verb but is the noun: J. M. Barrie's stage play. Hammer, like pan, means review savagely.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Pan is J. M. Barrie's 1904 stage drama about the boy who never grew up.

clue.text: Zonked Handel saw dandelions 11 Across 20 Down

indicators.note: zonked means dazed or stupefied, so these letters are scrambled into new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A dazed Handel stares at the dandelions on the lawn.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the answer to the other linked clue, the phrase about the close of day.
explanation.definitionFit: Both stock phrases mean ultimately, once everything has been taken into account, so they are interchangeable idioms.

clue.text: Prodigy at first ignored in class

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the word beside it
placing something in another word means it goes inside that word

blocks.note: the opening letter of this word
a genus is a class in biological classification

explanation.surface: A gifted child overlooked by teachers in the classroom.
explanation.walkthrough: Class is the biological sense, a group of species.
explanation.definitionFit: A prodigy is a person of exceptional talent, the same idea as a person of extraordinary brilliance.

clue.text: See 11
Moving south east, wise person is getting on

indicators.note: south is S, and moving it east in an across answer sends it rightwards to the end

blocks.note: a sage is a wise person

explanation.surface: A wise old person relocating to the south-east as they get older.
explanation.walkthrough: Moving south east reads as a house move, but it shifts the S of SAGE to the right-hand end.
explanation.definitionFit: To age is to grow older, so someone who ages is getting on in years.

clue.text: Fine athletes trained to save energy set out at night

indicators.note: to save something is to keep it in, so one piece is held within the rest
training reshapes and drills, so these letters are put into a new order

blocks.note: F is the pencil-grading abbreviation for fine
taken as written
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: Fit athletes conserving their strength before heading out for an evening run.
explanation.walkthrough: Set out at night looks like setting off, but a set is a set of dentures, laid out in a glass at bedtime.
explanation.definitionFit: Dentures come as a set and are removed and placed in water before sleep, a whimsical descriptive definition.

clue.text: Stop harnessing atomic energy

indicators.note: a harness straps around something, so one piece is fitted inside another

blocks.note: to stem a flow is to stop it
A is a standard abbreviation for atomic

explanation.surface: A call to halt the use of nuclear power.
explanation.walkthrough: Atomic energy looks like one phrase, but atomic supplies a letter and energy alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Steam means vigour or momentum, as in running out of steam, and is also literally a power source.

clue.text: Plastic bricks on order initially

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter of the word before is kept

blocks.note: in cricket the on side is also called the leg side, the batter's legward half of the field
the opening letter of this word

explanation.surface: Toy building blocks arriving first in an order.
explanation.walkthrough: On is a cricket term: the on side of the field, where the batter stands, is the leg side.
explanation.definitionFit: Lego is the Danish brand of interlocking toy building blocks moulded from coloured plastic.

clue.text: Inaccurate summary in Times exposed

indicators.note: something exposed has its covering stripped, so the outer letters go and the middle stays
placing something in another word means it sits inside that word

blocks.note: a précis is a short summary
the newspaper's name with its first and last letters removed

explanation.surface: A newspaper reports an error, revealing a misleading summary in its pages.
explanation.walkthrough: Times is italicised as the newspaper's title, but only its inner letters are used.
explanation.definitionFit: Imprecise means lacking exactness, so it is a direct synonym of inaccurate or not correct.

clue.text: Water nymph heard near a delta

indicators.note: heard tells us it is the sound of the words that counts, not their spelling

blocks.note: nigh means near; D is delta in the radio alphabet

explanation.surface: A spirit of the water is said to live close to a river mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: Delta suggests a river mouth, apt for a nymph, but here it is the NATO alphabet's D.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek mythology a naiad is a female spirit presiding over a spring, river or fountain.

clue.text: Capital once managed by board

blocks.note: to run a business is to manage it
to board a ship or train is to go on it

explanation.surface: Money that a company's directors once controlled.
explanation.walkthrough: Capital suggests money and board a company's directors, but here they are a city and a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Rangoon, now Yangon, was the capital of Burma, later Myanmar, until the government moved to Naypyidaw in 2006.

clue.text: Style with pen shown in Blaise perhaps

blocks.note: a mode is a manner or style
a sty is a pen for pigs

explanation.surface: A writer's flair with a pen on display in the work of Blaise Pascal, say.
explanation.walkthrough: Pen suggests writing, but here it is an animal enclosure. Modesty Blaise is a British comic-strip heroine created by Peter O'Donnell.
explanation.definitionFit: Blaise is the surname of the spy-adventuress, so her first name completes the character's name in a playful definition.
